insights.claim: All seven admission webhooks use failurePolicy: Fail, creating a hard dependency on webhook availability for Spark workload submission.
insights.reasoning: The analyzer extracted 7 distinct admission webhooks (4 mutating, 3 validating) all with failurePolicy Fail. This means webhook downtime blocks all SparkApplication, ScheduledSparkApplication, SparkConnect creation and updates, and all pod creation in namespaces matching the webhook selector. This is a deliberate correctness-over-availability trade-off but creates an operational concern for platform operators.

insights.claim: The webhook dynamically reads the OpenShift APIServer TLS profile at startup to align its cipher configuration with the cluster-wide security policy.
insights.reasoning: The webhook reads config.openshift.io/v1/APIServer named 'cluster' and parses its TLS profile to configure the webhook server's minimum TLS version and cipher suites. This pattern ensures the operator respects cluster-wide TLS hardening policies set by platform administrators. On non-OpenShift clusters, it gracefully falls back to TLS 1.2 minimum. This is relevant to cross-component TLS consistency across the RHOAI platform.

insights.claim: The spark-operator-module implements the odh-platform-utilities common.PlatformObject interface, enabling uniform lifecycle management by the ODH Operator.
insights.reasoning: The SparkOperator CR type satisfies common.PlatformObject via compile-time check (var _ common.PlatformObject = &SparkOperator{}), embedding common.ManagementSpec and common.Status. This pattern is shared across RHOAI module operators and enables the central ODH Operator to manage component lifecycle, status, and conditions through a uniform interface. Components using this pattern can be enabled/disabled via ManagementState.
